name: MODE.MULT
description: MODE.MULT returns a vertical array of all values that occur with the greatest frequency in a dataset, so it can report multiple modes at once.
tldr: Returns every value tied for the highest frequency as an array.

parameters.name: number1
parameters.description: The first number, cell, or range to evaluate.

basicExample.description: Two values share the top frequency
basicExample.explanation: Both 2 and 3 occur twice, more than 1 and 4, so both are returned.

advancedExamples.title: Three tied modes
advancedExamples.description: When more than two values tie, all are returned.
advancedExamples.explanation: Each of 7, 8, and 9 occurs twice, so all three are returned.

advancedExamples.title: Single mode still returns an array
advancedExamples.description: Even with one mode the result is a one-element array.
advancedExamples.explanation: 5 occurs three times; it is returned as a single-element array.

howItWorks: MODE.MULT finds the highest frequency among the numeric values, then returns every value that reaches that frequency. It returns a vertical (column) array, so in modern Excel it spills into multiple cells; in older versions it must be entered as a multi-cell array formula with Ctrl+Shift+Enter. If no value repeats, it returns #N/A. Text, logical values, and empty cells are ignored.

howToSteps.name: Select a vertical range of cells
howToSteps.text: Highlight enough empty cells below the formula cell to hold all modes.

howToSteps.name: Enter the formula
howToSteps.text: Type =MODE.MULT(range) in the top cell of the selection.

howToSteps.name: Confirm as array (older Excel)
howToSteps.text: In Excel 2019 and earlier press Ctrl+Shift+Enter; in Microsoft 365 just press Enter to spill.

limitations: Returns a vertical array, so it needs multiple cells to display all modes (or dynamic-array spill in Microsoft 365).
Returns #N/A when every value is unique.
Ignores text labels, so repeated category names are not counted.

commonErrors.cause: No value is repeated in the data.
commonErrors.fix: Use MODE.SNGL or verify the dataset contains duplicates.

commonErrors.cause: Formula entered in a single cell without array handling in pre-365 Excel.
commonErrors.fix: Select a vertical range of cells and confirm with Ctrl+Shift+Enter.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: Google Sheets does not have MODE.MULT; the closest is MODE which returns only one mode.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Sheets returns a single value (2). To get all modes use ARRAYFORMULA with a frequency helper or a custom approach.

faq.question: Why do I only see one result?
faq.answer: In older Excel the formula must be entered as an array across several cells. In Microsoft 365 it spills automatically.

faq.question: How is MODE.MULT different from MODE.SNGL?
faq.answer: MODE.SNGL returns one mode (lowest on ties); MODE.MULT returns all tied modes as an array.

faq.question: What if there is no repeated value?
faq.answer: MODE.MULT returns #N/A because no mode exists.
